Chroma is a syntax highlighting library and command-line tool that takes source code and other structured text and converts it into syntax highlighted HTML, ANSI-coloured text, and other formats.

## Try it

## Command-line Interface

A command-line interface to Chroma is included.

Binaries are available to install from [the releases page](https://github.com/alecthomas/chroma/releases).

### Usage with `less`

The CLI can be used as a preprocessor to colorise output of `less(1)`,
see documentation for the `LESSOPEN` environment variable.

The `--fail` flag can be used to suppress output and return with exit status
1 to facilitate falling back to some other preprocessor in case chroma
does not resolve a specific lexer to use for the given file. For example:

```shell
export LESSOPEN='| p() { chroma --fail "$1" || cat "$1"; }; p "%s"'
```

Replace `cat` with your favourite fallback preprocessor.

When invoked as `.lessfilter`, the `--fail` flag is automatically turned
on under the hood for easy integration with [lesspipe shipping with
Debian and derivatives](https://manpages.debian.org/lesspipe#USER_DEFINED_FILTERS);
for that setup the `chroma` executable can be just symlinked to `~/.lessfilter`.

### Usage with `less`

The CLI can be used as a preprocessor to colorise output of `less(1)`,
see documentation for the `LESSOPEN` environment variable.

The `--fail` flag can be used to suppress output and return with exit status
1 to facilitate falling back to some other preprocessor in case chroma
does not resolve a specific lexer to use for the given file. For example:

```shell
export LESSOPEN='| p() { chroma --fail "$1" || cat "$1"; }; p "%s"'
```

Replace `cat` with your favourite fallback preprocessor.

When invoked as `.lessfilter`, the `--fail` flag is automatically turned
on under the hood for easy integration with [lesspipe shipping with
Debian and derivatives](https://manpages.debian.org/lesspipe#USER_DEFINED_FILTERS);
for that setup the `chroma` executable can be just symlinked to `~/.lessfilter`.

## Projects using Chroma

* [`moor`](https://github.com/walles/moor) is a full-blown pager that colorizes
  its input using Chroma
* [Hugo](https://gohugo.io/) is a static site generator that [uses Chroma for syntax
  highlighting code examples](https://gohugo.io/content-management/syntax-highlighting/)

    r=subprocess.run(args, input=stdin_data, capture_output=True, text=True)
    out = r.stdout
    if len(out) > 3000:
        out = out[:3000] + f"...[len={len(out)}]"
    print(f"CMD: {' '.join(args)}")
    print(f"  stdin={stdin_data!r}")
    print(f"  stdout={out!r}")
    print(f"  stderr={r.stderr[:2000]!r}")
    print(f"  rc={r.returncode}\n")

# html tab width
run(['./executable','-l','python','-s','monokai','--html','--html-only','--html-tab-width=4'], stdin_data='a\tb\n')
run(['./executable','-l','python','-s','monokai','--html','--html-only','--html-tab-width=2'], stdin_data='a\tb\n')
# html lines
run(['./executable','-l','python','-s','monokai','--html','--html-only','--html-lines'], stdin_data='print(1)\nprint(2)\n')
run(['./executable','-l','python','-s','monokai','--html','--html-only','--html-lines','--html-lines-table'], stdin_data='print(1)\nprint(2)\n')

run(['./executable','-l','python','-s','monokai','--html','--html-only','--html-highlight=1:2'], stdin_data='print(1)\nprint(2)\n')
# base line
run(['./executable','-l','python','-s','monokai','--html','--html-only','--html-lines','--html-base-line=5'], stdin_data='print(1)\nprint(2)\n')
# prevent surrounding pre
run(['./executable','-l','python','-s','monokai','--html','--html-only','--html-prevent-surrounding-pre'], stdin_data='print("hi")\n')
# linkable lines
run(['./executable','-l','python','-s','monokai','--html','--html-only','--html-lines','--html-linkable-lines'], stdin_data='print(1)\n')
PY"}

from pygments.lexers import get_lexer_by_name
from pygments import lex
from pygments.token import Token

def chroma_tokens(code, lexer):
    r=subprocess.run(['./executable','-l',lexer,'-s','monokai','-f','tokens'], input=code, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout

def pyg_tokens(code, lexer_name):
    lexer = get_lexer_by_name(lexer_name)
    out=[]
    for t,v in lex(code, lexer):
        # map to chroma name: Token.Name.Builtin -> NameBuiltin
        name=str(t).replace('Token.','').replace('.','')
        # special? Token.Text.Whitespace -> TextWhitespace (no dot)
        out.append((name, v))
    return out

# test python whitespace handling
for code in ['  \n', '\n', '    ', 'a b\n', 'def foo():\n    pass\n']:
    print(f"=== CODE {code!r} ===")
    print("CHROMA:")
    print(chroma_tokens(code, 'python'), end='')
    print("PYGMENTS:")
    for n,v in pyg_tokens(code, 'python'):
        print(f"  {n!r} {v!r}")
    print()
PY"}

from pygments.lexers import get_lexer_by_name
from pygments import lex

def chroma_tokens(code, lexer):
    r=subprocess.run(['./executable','-l',lexer,'-s','monokai','-f','tokens'], input=code, capture_output=True, text=True)
    # parse &Token{Type, "value"} lines
    import re
    toks=[]
    for line in r.stdout.strip().split('\n'):
        if not line: continue
        m=re.match(r'&Token\{([^,]+), "(.*)"\}', line)
        # need to unescape? value is Go-quoted? e.g., "\"hi\"" -> need to decode?
        # For now just raw
        if m:
            toks.append((m.group(1), m.group(2)))
        else:
            toks.append(('PARSEFAIL', line))
    return toks

    lexer = get_lexer_by_name(lexer_name)
    raw=[]
    for t,v in lex(code, lexer):
        name=str(t).replace('Token.','').replace('.','')
        raw.append((name, v))
    # coalesce same-type adjacent
    coalesced=[]
    for n,v in raw:
        if coalesced and coalesced[-1][0]==n:
            coalesced[-1]=(n, coalesced[-1][1]+v)
        else:

import subprocess
def auto(code):
    r=subprocess.run(['./executable','-s','monokai','-f','tokens'], input=code, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout.strip()
def expl(code, lex):
    r=subprocess.run(['./executable','-l',lex,'-s','monokai','-f','tokens'], input=code, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return r.stdout.strip()

# distinguish GDScript3 vs Pony

    a=auto(code)
    g=expl(code,'GDScript3')
    p=expl(code,'Pony')
    print(f"code {code!r}")
    print(f"  auto: {a[:100]!r}")
    print(f"  gd3 : {g[:100]!r} match={a==g}")
    print(f"  pony: {p[:100]!r} match={a==p}")

            if stripped == 'lexers:':

            current = {'name': stripped, 'aliases': [], 'filenames': [], 'mimetypes': []}

def levenshtein(a, b):
    # standard DP
    if a == b:

    la, lb = len(a), len(b)
    if la == 0:

    if lb == 0:
